reviews.reasons: The single member (overflow tent installs) has every link established by the card's EVIDENCE: four WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements at $1,600 each (state AGREED) are real purchase prices from these buyers; the fulfiller is the recorded one, Summit Event Crews LLC, on a written $1,000-per-install quote; card exposure $0; usable cash 10 days after install. Arithmetic recomputed: 4 x $1,600 = $6,400 collected >= $4,500 (3 installs alone = $4,800 also clears it); subcontract 4 x $1,000 = $4,000 < price, paid from collected receipts so capital out stays $0 <= $1,000 cap; net $2,400; install day 5 + 10 = settled day 15 of 40. Metric is settled cash collected, so the $4,000 subcontract outflow does not reduce the target. Both excluded openings are correctly excluded: security staffing has no named or quoted fulfiller (FULFILMENT missing) and the workbook's $350 is only the owner's word (PERSON), so neither may count. EXECUTABLE is the right stance.
findings: The install dates of the four signed orders are not on the card; the plan places them on day 5. Even if installs slipped to day 30 the 10-day settlement still lands by day 40, but any install after day 30 would push its cash out of the window; Brain should confirm the dates in step s1.
SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED: setup needed before s1/s3, not an evidential gap.

If Summit requires payment before the rental companies pay, four concurrent installs would need $4,000 > the $1,000 cap; the card's EVIDENCE exposure of $0 says it does not, and the plan relies on that fact.
